jobs.title: Research Intern, Frontier Agents (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Role The Agents team investigates how to build, align, and scale frontier AI systems that can tackle complex, multi-step tasks and workflows across text and speech, with a particular focus on agentic and scientific domains. Our work sits at the intersection of agent capabilities, human-computer interaction, and infrastructure—from designing post-training methods for agentic behavior to developing evaluation frameworks for open-ended tasks where traditional metrics fall short. As a research intern, you will work on problems at the frontier of agentic AI, where challenges in alignment, reliability, and scalability are deeply intertwined. Projects may involve developing new training recipes for self-learning and long-horizon reasoning, curating datasets for non-deterministic scientific and agentic tasks, studying failure modes in agentic behavior, or building infrastructure that enables agent operations at scale. You'll operate in a space where algorithmic innovation, dataset and interaction design, and systems work come together to push the boundaries of what AI agents can reliably accomplish. Responsibilities Research and implement novel techniques in one or more of our focus areas Design and conduct rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses Document findings in scientific publications and blog posts Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team Requirements Currently pursuing a Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering

jobs.title: Research Intern, Frontier Speculative Decoding (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About the Role The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation. As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic. Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic. jobs.title: Research Intern, Inference (Summer 2027)
jobs.description_text: About The Role The Inference Research team is dedicated to building the next generation of efficient, scalable, and reliable serving systems for large foundation models, directly contributing to the mission of advancing open and transparent AI. Our work operates at the critical intersection of cutting-edge model architectures, high-performance systems engineering, and deep hardware optimization. We focus on co-designing software, algorithms, and models to significantly lower the cost and latency of modern AI systems. As a research intern, you will dive into the complexities of distributed inference, compiler-aware optimization, and novel inference-time computation strategies (such as speculative decoding and phase-aware execution). You will be tasked with co-designing and implementing cross-layer optimizations across models, systems, and hardware, with a focus on areas like KV cache design and large-scale serving architectures. Projects aim to unlock unprecedented performance and scale for foundation models, enabling faster serving, larger model deployment (e.g., Mixture-of-Experts), and robust, reproducible evaluation under realistic serving workloads. You’ll work across two areas: Infrastructure Agent Systems — Build production AI agents that help operate our GPU fleet by diagnosing failures, investigating incidents, gathering evidence from live systems, and assisting with remediation. jobs.title: (Staff / Senior Staff) AI Infra Engineer, Inference Infrastructure
jobs.description_text: About The Role We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page. The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. We design and build everything from bespoke satellites to full constellations, supported by vertically integrated, in‑house components that enable speed, precision, and constant innovation. As the Head of Mission Design & Flight Dynamics, you will lead the discipline across all missions and locations, spanning analysis, development, and operations. This role could be based in New Zealand or the U.S. WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO: Own the vision and direction of the Mission Design & Flight Dynamics technology roadmap, balancing live mission delivery with long-term capability growth. Drive measurable progress toward greater automation, efficiency, and expanded operational capability. Provide mentorship, clarity of vision, prioritisation, and motivation to the Flight Dynamics team during development phases and operational campaigns. Lead a global multi-site team, supported by regional Team Leads who manage day-to-day execution. Focus on strategic leadership, technical forecasting, emergent risk response, and cross-functional decision making. Maintain strong technical awareness across interfaces including Spacecraft Operations, FSW, GNC, GSW, and Systems

jobs.title: Incoming Quality Control Inspector - Mechanical
jobs.description_text: NEUTRON Neutron is a medium lift launch vehicle capable of delivering the mega constellations of tomorrow, high assurance payloads, and human spaceflight. As a highly reusable launch platform, Neutron will deliver a highly cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab’s proven execution history with the Electron program. If you’re interested in joining a high performing team, pushing the boundaries with a clean sheet development of re-usable liquid launch vehicle, this is your opportunity! ABOUT INCOMING QUALITY CONTROL INSPECTOR AT ROCKET LAB As an Incoming Quality Control (IQC) Inspector - Mechanical, you're the gate between our suppliers and our production floor. When hardware arrives, whether it's a machined manifold, a 3D-printed injector, or a batch of fasteners, you verify that it matches the drawing, the purchase order, and the paperwork before it goes anywhere near an engine or stage. If it's right, you release it. If it's not, you quarantine it, write it up, and make sure it doesn't come back the same way twice WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO: Inspect a wide range of hardware , including purchased parts, 3D-printed components, CNC-machined parts, and electro-mechanical assemblies, against drawings, specifications, and purchase order requirements. jobs.title: Inventory Coordinator
jobs.description_text: ABOUT INVENTORY COORDINATOR AT ROCKET LAB Rockets don't get built without the right parts. As Rocket Lab's Inventory Coordinator, you'll manage thousands of components and hundreds of orders, delivering them just-in-time to the teams who need them. You'll help Operations hit daily and weekly production targets, adapt quickly when priorities shift, and champion DIFOT (Delivery in Full, On Time) performance. If you thrive on precision, pace, and problem-solving, this is your chance to play a hands-on role in space. In this role, you will provide day-to-day IT support, interact positively with staff, and play a key role in onboarding new hires to ensure productivity from day one. jobs.title: Junior Development Engineer - Neutron
jobs.description_text: While other companies talk about it, we do it! NEUTRON Rocket Lab’s Neutron team is responsible for bringing our new large rocket Neutron and its launch and test sites to life. From designing and testing Neutron’s structures and components, to firing up its new Archimedes engines, to setting up Neutron’s launch pads and test sites across the United States, joining the Neutron team is your opportunity to help launch a new large rocket for the very first time. DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER II Development Engineers deliver across a broad set of vehicle domains including structural ( i.e. Propellant tanks, interstages , fairings) , mechanical (i.e. stage separation, landing, aerodynamic control) , fluid (i.e. pressurant , propellant management, ignition, HVAC), and thermal (i.e. thermal protection) systems. This role will focus on vehicle structures, working closely with analysis and manufacturing engineers to h elp support the development of concepts, detailed designs, and drawing packages for metallic and composites components & assemblies. This role requires close work with more experienced engineers to deliver project contribution to the expectations of the company. jobs.title: Junior Ground Systems Engineer - Instrumentation & Control
jobs.description_text: ABOUT INSTRUMENTATION & CONTROL AT ROCKET LAB: At Rocket Lab, we're not just launching rockets, we're building the future of space. Our Terrestrial Software team, including Instrumentation & Control, is at the heart of this mission. We design, build, and operate the critical software and control systems that power our ground infrastructure from launch pads, transporters, and erectors to the test stands where our engines are proven before flight. Every launch and engine test depends on the automated control and instrumentation systems our team delivers. As part of Terrestrial Software, you’ll help create and maintain the systems that enable Rocket Lab to build world-class facilities and launch vehicles faster than ever before. Your expertise will drive both operational excellence and innovative design, ensuring our Electron and Neutron vehicles reach new heights. jobs.title: Junior Radio Frequency Engineer - Test
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Every Rocket Lab launch depends on Radio Frequency (RF) communications and navigation systems that perform the first time, every time. The RF team designs, qualifies and supports the radio systems that keep our launch vehicles connected to the ground, from telemetry and command links to navigation. Based in our Auckland Production Complex, the Junior RF Engineer - Test will help make sure every RF component and system that flies on our vehicles has been properly tested, qualified and accepted. You'll plan and run qualification and acceptance tests, build the test rigs and automation that make those tests accurate and repeatable, and support production teams as they integrate RF hardware into flight vehicles. This is an entry-level role. You'll work closely with experienced RF systems engineers who will guide your work and review it. You'll also get hands-on with real flight hardware from day one. It's a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines, and it's a great place to build deep, practical RF test experience quickly. WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO: Develop qualification and acceptance test plans for RF components and systems, with guidance from senior engineers. Perform qualification and acceptance testing, and write clear test reports that document the results. Design and build test rigs for component qualification and acceptance testing, including hardware-in-the-loop test equipment. Develop novel test methods for radio components and systems. jobs.title: Junior Software Engineer
jobs.description_text: WHAT YOU'LL GET TO DO: As part of the Production Automation team you will work with a supportive, international team of software developers with diverse engineering backgrounds. A typical day consists of collaborating with avionics and manufacturing engineers to develop, improve and support software-applications to functionally test spacecraft-components and systems for our launch vehicles (Electron, Neutron) and Space-System programs. You will work closely with our stakeholders during both the development phase of new components and when those components move to a production line. Our team is involved in the test rig bring-up process and rig maintenance and assists the engineering teams with evaluating test result data. We're after developers willing to take on new challenges. Even if you don't have our tech stack fully covered, we'd still want to hear from you! YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS: Tertiary Diploma, Certificate or degree in Software-/Electrical-/Mechatronics-Engineering, Computer Science or demonstrated equivalent level of knowledge Proficient in English DESIRABLE SKILLS: Experience with Python, C++ or similar Comfortable working in a Linux development environment THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE: Interest in embedded systems Experience/Interest in basic electronics If the above sounds like you, apply now!
